Brin attended Trump's inauguration and contributed hundreds of thousands of dollars to the Republican National Committee in 2025. Huang donated to a fund to build Trump's White House ballroom, and Nvidia contributed $1 million to Trump's inauguration ceremony. Dell is a longtime Trump donor. Along with his wife Susan, he committed $6.25 billion to seed Trump Accounts designed to jumpstart savings for children in the U.S. AMD is also contributing to Trump funds. headlines.title: Anthropic will be 'most ridiculous IPO' of year, analyst says
headlines.summary: Anthropic reportedly plans to list on the Nasdaq before Thanksgiving, and one bearish advisory firm suggests that investors sit this one out.
headlines.article_text: Anthropic will be 'most ridiculous IPO' of year, analyst says Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Research firm New Constructs wrote in a note on Tuesday that Anthropic's IPO would be "the most ridiculous IPO of 2026," posing a historic risk to financial markets. Anthropic is reportedly seeking a $2 trillion valuation in its upcoming Nasdaq listing. The company's growing operating losses, combined with the rise in popularity of open-source models, leaves Anthropic without a "viable business," according to the report. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei speaks during the keynote address at Salesforce's Dreamforce conference at the Moscone Center on Sept. 15, 2026 in San Francisco, California. Benjamin Fanjoy | Getty Images As Anthropic barrels toward a potential $2 trillion market cap on the Nasdaq, one research firm is valuing the artificial intelligence company at a mere $150 billion and says Wall Street is about to face an "unprecedented test of investor gullibility." In a report on Tuesday, independent financial research provider New Constructs called Anthropic's upcoming offering the "most ridiculous IPO of 2026." To reach its desired valuation, the firm estimates Anthropic would need to record double the trailing year of profit for Nvidia , the world's most valuable tech company. Nvidia's net income over the past four quarters topped $190 billion. Meanwhile, Anthropic's revenue in 2025 was $4.6 billion as the company racked up a net loss of $42 billion, according to Reuters , which cited a leaked copy of the company's prospectus. Anthropic's mounting operating losses coupled with emerging competition from a plethora of open-source models led New Constructs to conclude that, "We don't think Anthropic has a viable business." "Since the arrival of open-source models, it's been clear that the closed models would struggle to generate profits," the firm wrote. David Trainer, founder and CEO of New Constructs, has built a reputation on Wall Street as a notorious bear on IPOs. He's been right in the past. New Constructs called WeWork "the most ridiculous IPO of 2019," ahead of the office-sharing company's planned offering. WeWork had been valued privately at $47 billion, but just six weeks after the New Constructs report, the company pulled its IPO amid weak demand and intense criticism surrounding its financials. WeWork filed for bankruptcy in 2023. "While Anthropic offers more to society than WeWork ever did, at a $2 trillion valuation, its IPO presents far bigger risks and is positioned to be a far bigger rip off of U.S. capital markets," New Constructs wrote, adding that the IPO's purpose isn't to provide wealth for public markets investors, but rather liquidity for the company's Wall Street backers. Anthropic didn't respond to a request for comment. New Constructs was also bearish on Allbirds ' IPO in 2021. The shoe company debuted on the Nasdaq and reached a valuation of $4.1 billion on its opening day. Earlier this year, the company sold its assets to American Exchange Group for an estimated $39 million, pivoting to AI in the process. Trainer's firm has also missed the mark on calls. Its "most ridiculous" 2020 IPO choice was DoorDash , which the firm also compared to WeWork, calling the food delivery company "similarly disadvantaged." However, DoorDash has held up on the public market. The stock shot up on its first day in December 2020, giving the company a market cap of over $60 billion. That number has since swelled to $83 billion. In an interview with CNBC in 2021, Trainer acknowledged that "crazy stuff happens" and New Constructs doesn't always get it right. "I can't let that bother me," he said at the time. "I have to stay true to what I think is right." Anthropic still hasn't made its prospectus public, so New Constructs hasn't seen the actual filing. However, the firm cited figures that have been reported, including from the New York Times, which reported in September that the company was on pace to generate $100 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026. Anthropic claimed at the end of July that its annualized revenue run rate was up sevenfold year-over-year to $65 billion. The New Constructs report also notes that Anthropic's assertion that AI could pose "a catastrophic or existential risk to humanity" is another reason why investors should avoid the IPO. "While we were not fortunate enough to be one of the few to whom Anthropic's S-1 was selectively disclosed, the reports of the leaked financials reveal more than enough to assess the gargantuan risks of investing in this IPO," New Constructs wrote. headlines.article_text: Lululemon poaches Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger as chief product officer Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Lululemon announced Wednesday that Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger has is joining the company as its chief product officer, a newly created role. The announcement comes just a month after Heidi O'Neill took over the company as CEO. Athleta owner Gap told CNBC in a statement that the leadership transition will allow it to accelerate its work in repositioning the brand for growth. In this article LULU GAP Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Shoppers enter a Lululemon store in Walnut Creek, California, July 15, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Lululemon announced Wednesday that Athleta CEO Maggie Gauger is joining the company as president and chief product officer, effective later this month. The move marks the latest shake-up among the top executives in the increasingly competitive athleisure space: Gauger joined Athleta from Nike only last year. Lululemon said Gauger's job is a newly created role. It also appointed Joseph Godsey as chief operating officer. Alongside the new announcements, Lululemon also said Nikki Neuburger, the company's chief brand and product activation officer, and Ted Dagnese, its chief supply chain officer, are leaving in November to "pursue other opportunities." "We are establishing a deeply experienced leadership team that will work in a more coordinated manner, aligned around the strategy and execution that delivers the most impact for our guests, our communities, and our business," Lululemon CEO Heidi O'Neill said in a statement. "That starts with putting product, design, and innovation at the center of how we operate, with the focus and accountability to create a stronger pipeline of differentiated product to raise the bar for our guests across every touchpoint, in stores and online." In a statement provided to CNBC, Athleta parent company Gap confirmed Gauger has left the company. It said Erika Everett, the brand's current chief marketing officer, will oversee the brand CEO role in the interim. "We have been actively shaping Athleta's next chapter and the changes needed to position the brand for long-term growth," Gap said in its statement. "This transition enables us to accelerate that work, strengthen our connection with customers, and unlock Athleta's full potential." Separately, Lululemon said it is also searching for a chief brand officer, a chief communications officer and a chief technology officer. O'Neill took the helm of Lululemon last month after the athleisure company saw more than a year of disappointing sales performance in the midst of a proxy battle, drawing criticism from founder Chip Wilson. headlines.summary: Since SpaceX's record-breaking IPO in June, rates have sold off, and yields on its bonds have risen, along with other AI-related bonds.
headlines.article_text: SpaceX in talks with Apollo, banks to back $40B Nvidia chip buy Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apollo Capital and several banks are in talks with SpaceX to facilitate the $40 billion purchase of Nvidia GPUs, a source told CNBC. The deal will primarily rely on the investment-grade debt market. Discussions are preliminary and details have yet to be finalized, including key lenders. In this article SPCX NVDA APO Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 2:13 02:13 SpaceX in talks with Apollo, consortium of banks to support $40 billion purchase of Nvidia GPUs Squawk on the Street Apollo Capital Management and several banks are in discussions with SpaceX to help facilitate the company's purchase of $40 billion worth of Nvidia graphics processing units, according to a person familiar with the talks who asked not to be named to discuss the matter. The deal will primarily rely on the investment-grade debt market, which SpaceX just tapped four months ago, the person said. Two weeks after its record-breaking IPO in mid-June, the space exploration company raised $25 billion in bonds at different durations. CNBC was told at the time that SpaceX's bond sale saw incredibly high demand, highlighting strong interest from fixed-income investors. But since then, artificial intelligence-related bonds have sold off, while credit spreads have widened. SpaceX's $40 billion debt deal will likely use GPUs as collateral and Apollo Capital is said to be playing a leading role in facilitating the financing, the person said. Apollo declined to comment. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The market is still operating under the expectation that GPUs hold their value for about seven years, according to a person in the credit industry who asked not to be named to discuss the matter. Computing power is scarce and the shortage is not expected to abate anytime soon, which supports the value of high-performing GPUs. The Financial Times was first to report on the financing talks. Read more CNBC tech news Google ordered to halt work on two data centers in 'Texas of Europe' Meta joins with group of companies to tame 'chaos' of doing business with AI bots Anduril lands $2.9 billion Navy submarine shipyard contract days after Luckey joins Pentagon weapons group Anthropic expands Claude Startups program in bid to snag founders and fast-growing companies While a bond deal of this size is notable, it follows a series of bond issuances from Meta , Amazon and Google as the cost to fund the AI buildout gets more expensive. Both sources told CNBC that more debt sales are expected, fixed-income investors are demanding a higher yield to service the debt, a sign that participants are becoming more selective about their AI exposure. SpaceX is already running a massive load of Nvidia AI chips and has plans to add to it. CEO Elon Musk said in a Sept. 24 post on X that his company's Colossus data center in Memphis, Tenn., was running 230,000 Nvidia AI chips, while Colossus 2 had 550,000. Musk said the company would more than double the number of chips by late December to reach 1.21 million, "If we get lucky." For the SpaceX bulls, the company has inked compute deals with Google, Anthropic , Reflection AI and Cursor, which it later bought, and bringing more capacity online could boost revenue quickly. On the flipside, the company reported nearly $40 billion in debt in its second-quarter financials, and its existing debt trades near junk bond levels, as credit markets have, overall, been more skittish. headlines.title: Microsoft to sell $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra containing Nvidia AI chip
headlines.summary: The new device shows Microsoft remains committed to making its own PCs even though it's not one of the top device makers.
headlines.article_text: Microsoft starts taking preorders for $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra contains an Nvidia chip that can run large AI models without generating cloud bills. The device contains a magnetic USB-C port similar to Apple's MagSafe charging connector. Microsoft also said that Meta will introduce its Muse AI agent for Windows. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Microsoft Windows Surface Laptop Ultra. Source: Microsoft Microsoft said its new laptop containing an Nvidia AI chip will start at $2,599, as the software maker tries to bring more artificial intelligence capabilities to its consumer devices. The Surface Laptop Ultra is now available on preorder and will begin shipping on Oct. 16, Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft's executive vice president of Windows and devices, said at a company event in San Francisco on Wednesday. The computer has the world's first magnetic USB-C port, similar to Apple's MagSafe charging connector, along with two other standard USB-C ports, Microsoft said in a blog post . While Microsoft Windows is the most popular operating system for PCs, the company isn't among the top six PC vendors in terms of unit shipments, according to an estimate from researcher Gartner. As the AI boom matures and chip technology advances, tech giants including Microsoft, Apple and Google are aiming to allow users to run more AI workloads from their devices rather than relying on the cloud. Users can install and run a variety of models on the new laptop without having to worry about racking up high monthly bills. Microsoft first talked about the Surface Laptop Ultra in May, but is just now providing specifics. "Microsoft might get me back to Windows," Max Weinbach, an analyst at Creative Strategies, wrote on X after the announcement. Davuluri also said that Meta will introduce a version of its popular Muse AI agent for Windows, capitalizing on the surging popularity of the personal agent, which has jumped to the top of Apple's App store, surpassing ChatGPT. Microsoft is still trying to solidify its role as a key player in AI. The company offers its own AI models, but they're less popular than leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic and aren't at the forefront in terms of performance, according to one benchmark . Developers are more likely to have used alternatives, according to a recent survey . This isn't the first time Microsoft has sought to use the AI boom as a way to boost sales of its devices. In 2024, the company introduced the Copilot+ PC standard, requiring the inclusion of neural processing units that ensure a minimum level of AI performance, along with compliant Surface computers. But Microsoft has since "simplified product naming to lead with the Surface brand, while continuing to deliver premium hardware and hybrid AI experiences," a spokesperson said. The new device sports a 15-inch display and weighs 4.4 pounds. It can contain up to 128 gigabytes of unified memory and supply up to one petaflop of computing power. The Blackwell RTX Spark GPU inside the computer has as much processing power as Nvidia's DGX-1 data center server from 2016, which cost $250 million, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at Wednesday's event. A presenter showed how apps on the Surface Laptop Ultra can route some AI coding requests run on the computer's local GPU, displaying a green leaf icon, and others to the cloud. Through Windows 11, developers can confine coding agents to Microsoft Execution Containers that will prevent unwanted system access. Microsoft is updating its Windows 11 device setup experience to help people get started quickly with open-source OpenClaw AI agent software. Microsoft has been releasing its own computers since 2012, and CEO Satya Nadella indicated on Tuesday that the company's position in the market is evolving. "I think today is the day we'll start talking and thinking about the frontier ecosystem taking maybe slightly different contours two years from now, five years from now, 10 years from now," Nadella said at the event. "That classic edge that distributed computing will always remain distributed will be more true."
